trust_decision.summary: Whether a request may read or mutate the Tilt HUD is decided by whether it carries the per-user session token (Tilt-Token cookie or X-Tilt-Token header) equal to EngineState.Token, plus an Origin check; at the pinned commit no HTTP HUD route decides anything and only the websocket's CheckOrigin guards /ws/view, accepting any request with no Origin header.

landing_point.why: The summary names the HUD websocket stream; CheckOrigin on the /ws/view upgrader is the only guard on that route, and it falls back to CheckSameOrigin, which returns true when the Origin header is absent.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is a different opt-in command (tilt snapshot view) serving a static file the developer chose to publish, with no live engine state and no session token in that process, so a solver can argue it was never part of the HUD server the advisory protects.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: tilt logs dials /ws/view with no csrf query parameter and no Origin header, relying on the CheckSameOrigin fallback; removing that fallback without teaching this client a token breaks 'tilt logs -f' (the published fix does not update it).

session token in the Tilt-Token cookie

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET / on the HUD catch-all handler sets Tilt-Token to the live session token for any unauthenticated caller, so requireToken can be satisfied by anyone who can reach the port
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The browser SPA needs the cookie on first page load and a cross-site page cannot read the response because of the same-origin policy, so it is not a token disclosure under the advisory's browser threat model
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package and same file as the route registration the fix touches

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The apiserver listener's non-/debug prefixes (/apis, /metrics, /healthz, /livez, /readyz, /openapi, /swagger, /version) carry no HUD token; only /debug was wrapped
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: That listener binds to 127.0.0.1 in the tilt-apiserver builder and /apis already requires the apiserver bearer token, so it is not remotely reachable
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point's controller hunk

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A token-gated route on the snapshot viewer's own ServeMux (e.g. /api/snapshot/local or an /api/view alias)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It reuses the same embedded asset server, serves the same serialized webview payload, and listens on the same --host flag (internal/cli/snapshot.go:127-128), so a maintainer treating it as 'the HUD in snapshot mode' would plausibly add the gate there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Sending the session token or fetched csrf token on the websocket Dial
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only other consumer of /ws/view in the tree; whoever tightens CheckOrigin must touch it, and the published fix shows exactly the omission a maintainer would make.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another sensitive PathPrefix mounted on the apiRouter (or on the webRouter) without the loopback/requireToken wrapper
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The router is a flat list of mounts; the fix added loopbackOnly to /debug only, so adding e.g. /metrics or /config the same way is an easy, natural sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second ProvideHeadsUpServerController construction wired to an empty &server.HeadsUpServer{} with a nil store
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This already exists (the headless server for 'tilt openapi'); a new middleware that reads s.store would nil-panic here, exactly as requireToken would on /proxy.
